# ffmpeg-render-pro

ffmpeg-render-pro is a Node.js toolkit that renders video from code in parallel. The user
(or agent) writes one function, renderFrame(frameNum, buffer), that paints raw BGRA pixels;
the toolkit splits the frame range across worker threads, encodes one MP4 segment per worker
through ffmpeg, joins the segments with stream copy (no re-encode), and serves a live
dashboard on 127.0.0.1. It also detects GPU encoders (NVENC, VideoToolbox, AMF, VA-API, QSV),
grades color, merges audio, and concatenates videos. Requires Node.js >= 18 and ffmpeg (on
PATH, or via FFMPEG_RENDER_PRO_FFMPEG). Version 1.5.2. MIT license.

## The three-step path (humans and agents)

1. Prove the setup: `npx ffmpeg-render-pro benchmark` (5 s test render, dashboard opens).
2. Get a worker: `npx ffmpeg-render-pro init my-worker.js`, or over MCP call get_worker_template
   and save its `starterSource` to a file. Edit renderFrame() only.
3. Render: `npx ffmpeg-render-pro render my-worker.js --duration=5`, or over MCP call
   render_video with worker_script set to that file.

Both bundled workers can be rendered as-is: starter-worker.js (gradient, edit-me file) and
basic-worker.js (particle test scene). get_worker_template returns both paths.

## Install

- No install: `npx ffmpeg-render-pro <command>`
- Global CLI + MCP binary: `npm install -g ffmpeg-render-pro`
- Library: `npm install ffmpeg-render-pro`
- Claude Code MCP: `claude mcp add --transport stdio ffmpeg-render-pro -- npx --yes --package=ffmpeg-render-pro ffmpeg-render-pro-mcp`

## MCP tools (7)

- get_worker_template: worker contract + starterSource/starterPath (edit renderFrame only) + templatePath (reference scene). Call first.
- render_video: parallel render from worker_script; duration required; fps default 30; progress notifications when the client sends a progressToken; client cancellation stops workers.
- detect_gpu: probe the best hardware encoder (re-probes each call, 7-day cache).
- system_info: CPU cores, RAM, recommended worker count for a resolution, ffmpeg version.
- color_grade: preset (noir, warm, cool, cinematic, vintage) or custom -vf filter.
- merge_audio: mux audio into video, video stream-copied, audio AAC, optional loop and loudnorm.
- concat_videos: stream-copy join; inputs probed with ffprobe by default.

All tools return structuredContent matching a declared outputSchema. Writers overwrite output_path.
stdout carries only JSON-RPC frames. For headless renders pass dashboard false and auto_open false.

## CLI

- `init [my-worker.js]` (--force overwrites), `benchmark`, `render <worker.js>`, `info`, `detect-gpu`, `version`
- Render flags: --width --height (even) --fps --duration --output --workers --max-workers --seed --title --crf --encoder-preset
- Dashboard flags: --no-dashboard --no-open --port --linger-ms (0 = exit when done)

## Worker contract

A worker runs as a worker_thread. workerData injects: width, height, fps, seed, startFrame,
endFrame (exclusive), segmentPath, workerId, totalFrames, duration, plus any extra keys from
renderParallel({ workerData }). The worker renders [startFrame, endFrame) to an MP4 at
segmentPath and posts to parentPort:

- { type: 'progress', workerId, pct, fps, frame, eta } periodically
- { type: 'done', workerId } once, after the segment is fully written
- { type: 'error', workerId, error } on failure (never done after error)
- { type: 'fast-forward-start', workerId, frames } optional, before replaying state

All segments must share codec, resolution, framerate, and pixel format. Derive all randomness
from seed for deterministic output.

## Library

require('ffmpeg-render-pro') exports renderParallel, createEncoder, detectGPU, getConfig,
computeTotalFrames, concatSegments, colorGrade, mergeAudio, startDashboard, ProgressTracker,
saveCheckpoint, loadCheckpoint, restoreCheckpoint, generateCheckpoints, getEncoderIO,
getCodecArgs, ffmpegBin, ffprobeBin. renderParallel options include signal (AbortSignal),
quiet (byte-clean stdout), and dashboardLingerMs (0 to return immediately).
